note: ADR-053 §1 / ADR-058 D2: a hand-written list of coherent scenarios grounded in how this product is ACTUALLY installed and used — never a Cartesian host x os x artifact matrix. Every machine-reachable scenario has structured proofs joining a workflow job to an exact existing test/driver path that the job invokes. Job-name existence alone is not evidence. Manual scenarios require a named owner and sit OUTSIDE the coverage denominator.

scenarios.stage: install — doctor on an absent/empty brain
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check — tests/integration/install-smoke.mjs: `--doctor` against an empty RUVNET_BRAIN_KB reports the diagnostic honestly (brain not found) and never crashes; read-only, the pinned dir is untouched afterward.

scenarios.stage: doctor on a COMPLETE brain — the healthy verdict must be derived, not hardwired
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check — tests/integration/install-smoke.mjs: `--doctor` on a complete brain dir (real stores + reader deps + mcp entrypoint present) returns exit 0, computed from those real files.

scenarios.stage: update — `--update` against a missing brain must fail LOUD, never silently no-op
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check & ci.yml#windows-unit — tests/integration/install-smoke.mjs: `--update` against an empty KB dir exits non-zero with the re-run-installer message.

scenarios.artifact: npm/github (re-run of the installer against an OLD installed brain)
scenarios.stage: update — the stale-install trap: a June-era brain must be detected as stale and re-fetched, and a newer-than-latest install must never be downgraded
scenarios.evidence: integration-linux.yml#integration — tests/integration/stale-install-trap.test.mjs: an installed OLD tag triggers a real re-download; a rate-limited/offline latest-check (source != 'latest') must not report a fabricated 'out of date' and downgrade an ahead-of-latest install.

scenarios.stage: install — Codex host present, no config.toml yet (issue #42 regression)
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check & ci.yml#windows-unit — tests/unit/codex-wiring.test.mjs: wireCodexHost() creates config.toml and registers [mcp_servers.ruvnet-brain] with a resolved absolute server path when ~/.codex exists but has no config yet.

scenarios.stage: install — the user's OWN pre-existing config.toml (other [mcp_servers.*] entries, comments, content after our block) must survive byte-for-byte
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check & ci.yml#windows-unit — tests/unit/codex-wiring.test.mjs: mergeCodexConfig preserves every pre-existing section byte-for-byte, leaves a user's own ruvnet-brain declaration alone, and preserves content the user added after our block.

scenarios.stage: update — reinstall/update must be idempotent (byte-identical on 2nd/3rd run) and must never widen the config file's permission mode
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check & ci.yml#windows-unit — tests/unit/codex-wiring.test.mjs: a second/third install run reproduces config.toml byte-for-byte, and a chmod-600 config never comes back world-readable.

scenarios.stage: install — a dotfiles-managed config.toml that is a SYMLINK must keep its identity
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check — tests/unit/codex-wiring.test.mjs: a symlinked config keeps its identity — the write goes THROUGH the link, never replacing it with a plain file.

scenarios.stage: install — an interrupted config write or server copy must leave the PRIOR bytes intact, never a torn file
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check — tests/unit/codex-wiring.test.mjs (failure-injection cases): a config-write or server-copy failure leaves the prior registration byte-intact (write-beside-then-rename), demonstrated to fail against the pre-fix plain copyFileSync/writeFileSync.

scenarios.artifact: npm tarball (packed, not the source checkout)
scenarios.stage: install — the published npm artifact must actually carry plugin/mcp/server.mjs (issue #43 regression: 20 files shipped, the Codex server was not one of them)
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check & ci.yml#windows-unit — tests/unit/npm-tarball-codex.test.mjs: `npm pack` + unpack proves plugin/mcp/server.mjs is IN the tarball, byte-identical to source, and no other plugin/ content leaks in.

scenarios.stage: first-query — the server installed FROM THE UNPACKED TARBALL (not the source tree) completes an MCP round trip and serves search_ruvnet
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check — tests/unit/npm-tarball-codex.test.mjs: initialize + tools/list succeed against the server copied from the real unpacked tarball, with the documented search_ruvnet schema (required string query, optional integer k).

scenarios.stage: hook-fire — the UserPromptSubmit grounding hook across on-topic/off-topic/malformed/empty/200KB/unicode/JSON-escaped/canary-injection prompts
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check — tests/unit/hook-battery.test.mjs: the 15-case ground-ruvnet.sh gate battery (playbook/grounding/hijack triggers, malformed & empty stdin, a 200KB prompt, unicode/emoji, JSON-escaped quotes, canary command substitutions) — every case exits 0.

scenarios.stage: recurring use — the session-start greeting must fire every session; the one-time star-ask must fire AT MOST once ever, across repeated sessions on the same HOME
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check — tests/unit/hook-battery.test.mjs: session-start.sh run twice with the same HOME — a sane greeting both times, star-ask appearing on the first eligible run and never again.

scenarios.stage: hook-fire under stress — four stdin regimes (valid JSON, empty EOF, 1MB garbage, held-open stdin past the declared timeout) under an external process-group watchdog
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check & ci.yml#windows-unit — tests/unit/selfcheck-battery.test.mjs: every hooks.json registration is driven through the real shim under all four stdin regimes; a genuinely hung hook is caught and killed by the process-group watchdog (an in-process timer cannot catch it).

scenarios.artifact: plugin + a user's own unrelated hooks
scenarios.stage: coexistence — our hooks must run alongside a stranger's own hooks (slow/failing/garbage-printing, before AND after ours) without ever executing theirs or altering their config
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check — tests/unit/selfcheck-battery.test.mjs coexistence suite: foreign hook registrations are enumerated and never executed.

scenarios.artifact: kb bundle (a REAL ~736MB downloaded + npm-installed brain, not a stub)
scenarios.stage: first-query — the core-capability battery must run for real, and a skip (absent brain, or cold embedder model) must become a HARD FAILURE, never a silent green
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#warm-brain — plugin/test/run-tests.mjs's capability battery, run with REQUIRE_BRAIN=1 against a real installed brain (ADR-058 D1); the SAME lane's mutant proof lives at ci.yml#check (tests/integration/require-brain-lane.mjs), which points RUVNET_BRAIN_KB at a deliberately empty dir.

scenarios.stage: install — the fast PR lane's non-fatal counterpart to S16: a fresh runner with no brain bundle must SKIP loudly, never silently, and must stay exit 0
scenarios.evidence: ci.yml#check — npm test (plugin/test/run-tests.mjs): the core-capability battery prints "CORE CAPABILITY BATTERY SKIPPED" and stays exit 0 when REQUIRE_BRAIN is unset, the honest counterpart to S16's hard failure.

scenarios.stage: install — native skills must be self-contained and visible through the real Codex plugin loader, and no shipped file may leak a developer's real home-directory path (the second defect ADR-051 found alongside issue #42)
scenarios.evidence: integration-linux.yml#integration — tests/integration/codex-skill-discovery.test.mjs installs the local marketplace into an isolated Codex home and proves brain-console + whats-new are discovered without broken sibling references; ci.yml#check — tests/unit/codex-wiring.test.mjs proves the retired skill.toml surface is absent and zero shipped files under .codex/ or plugin/ contain a real /Users/<account>/ path.

scenarios.stage: uninstall — `--uninstall` must reverse every footprint it left (plugin wiring, codex registration, brain cache, launchd/nightly state), never leaving orphaned config
scenarios.evidence: integration-linux.yml#integration — tests/integration/uninstall-footprint.test.mjs exercises the real --uninstall path and its footprint.

scenarios.stage: install — the full install + Codex/Claude-Code wiring journey on macOS
scenarios.evidence: stranger-matrix.yml#macos — scripts/ci/stranger-scenario.mjs installs the packed candidate into a virgin HOME, runs the assembled `--local` bundle path, verifies the installed package and Claude registries contain no automatic Brain hooks, and proves a seeded-broken bundle exits non-zero on macos-latest.

scenarios.artifact: local clone (`node bin/install.mjs --local`, assembled dist/ruvnet-brain/ directory)
scenarios.stage: install — the from-a-repo-clone path a contributor building the bundle locally takes
scenarios.evidence: stranger-matrix.yml#ubuntu/#macos/#windows-gitbash/#windows-powershell/#hostile — scripts/ci/stranger-scenario.mjs drives the real installer with `--local` against a freshly assembled directory on every matrix surface; healthy must prove automatic-hook retirement, seeded-broken must fail.

scenarios.artifact: packed npm artifact + assembled local bundle
scenarios.stage: install — hostile sh-only container with HOME containing spaces, no jq/gh, and outbound HTTP blackholed
scenarios.evidence: stranger-matrix.yml#hostile — scripts/ci/stranger-scenario.mjs installs into `/tmp/virgin home`, with sh only, jq/gh absent, proxy-blackholed network, and exercises healthy, seeded-broken, and strict-ungrounded outcomes.

scenarios.artifact: THE PUBLISHED SURFACE — npm registry (`npx ruvnet-brain@latest`) + the real GitHub Release bundle
scenarios.stage: post-publish — the artifact a stranger actually receives, checked on a clock rather than on a push
scenarios.evidence: published-surface-probe.yml#probe — nightly (cron '17 7 * * *', never on push) scripts/published-surface-probe.mjs: resolves the npm packument + dist-tags.latest, fetches a real byte range of the published tarball and asserts gzip magic, then INSTALLS AND EXECUTES `npx -y ruvnet-brain@latest --help` from the registry, and finally checks releases/latest carries ruvnet-brain.zip above a truncation floor, that its download URL serves the API-declared byte count, and that the .zip.sha256 sidecar is a well-formed 64-hex digest. RED when the package is unpublished, the tarball is not a gzip, the published CLI exits non-zero or prints someone else's help, the Release asset is missing/truncated/unfetchable, or the sidecar is malformed. A rate-limited or unreachable network is UNKNOWN (exit 4) and still red — never green-because-we-could-not-look. Every OTHER scenario in this list runs against the source checkout, which is a different artifact from the one a user receives; only a schedule can catch a surface that died without a commit.

scenarios.stage: install — hostile storage semantics not represented by the spaces/no-network cell: unicode HOME, read-only cache, or ENOSPC/near-full disk
scenarios.evidence: No committed workflow drives the installer through unicode HOME, read-only cache, or ENOSPC. S22 covers spaces and missing tools/network only; it is not evidence for these different filesystem failures.
